problem:
The number of subscribers $S(t)$ to a video channel after $t$ weeks can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0.05S.
$$

If the channel currently has $15\,000$ subscribers, calculate the number of subscribers after $12$ weeks. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
worked_solution:
We model the number of subscribers using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0.05S.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
S(t)={S}_{0}\,{e}^{0.05t},
$$

where ${S}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that the channel currently has $15\,000$ subscribers, so we have ${S}_{0}=15\,000.$

Therefore, the number of subscribers $S$ at time $t$ is

$$
S(t)=15\,000\,{e}^{0.05t}.
$$

Finally, to find the number of subscribers when $t=12,$ we substitute $t=12$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S(12) & =15\,000\,{e}^{0.05\cdot 12} \\  & =15\,000\,{e}^{0.6} \\  & ≈27\,331.78\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that the number of subscribers is $27\,332$ after $12$ weeks.
